newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end up on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end up on speculative buying.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Wednesday on speculative buying at low levels, traders said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at 3,409 yuan ($410) per tonne, rising 59 yuan. It opened at an intraday low of 3,350 and a high of 3,417.
May rose 10 to 3,360, September 45 to 3,445, November three to 3,438 and the January 1998 contract was unchanged at 3,440 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 16,700 tonnes from 11,600.
Soybeans opened mixed, mostly at their intraday lows and speculative buying pushed the prices steadily up for most of the session, traders said.

"Some retail investors dominated today's trading on optimistic expectations over the future market trend," one trader said. "They believe good fundamentals will support the futures prices in the short term."
Analysts said soybeans were more likely to rise than to fall in the next few days.
